name: buzz
one_liner: A self-hosted chat workspace, like Slack, but built so AI agents are full participants alongside humans — opening code changes, reviewing work, and posting updates in the same channels.
buyer: A small engineering team lead who wants their AI coding agents visible and auditable in the same place the humans already talk, instead of hidden in a separate tool.
business_use_cases: A dev team self-hosts it so AI agents post PR reviews and status updates directly into the team's channels, fully auditable.
An agency running multiple client projects uses one instance per client so both their staff and client-specific AI agents collaborate in one place.
A remote-first startup replaces a paid chat tool with this to also gain built-in agent workflow support.

money_ideas.idea: Managed hosting for teams that want the workspace without running their own relay.
Paid setup/integration service connecting a client's existing agents and repos into it.

steal_this: Self-host it this weekend for your own team, wire in one coding agent to post PR updates, and use the result as a demo to pitch managed hosting to other small teams.
